heroHeadline: UN Condemns Khan al-Ahmar Eviction as War Crime; Gaza Phase 2 Talks Collapse Over Hamas Disarmament; Settler Attack on Idhna
heroSubtitle: On June 4, 2026, the UN Committee on Palestinian Rights formally condemned Finance Minister Smotrich's order to evict and demolish Khan al-Ahmar — a Bedouin village in the strategic E1 corridor east of Jerusalem — as a war crime under international law; OHCHR simultaneously demanded Israel halt forcible displacement and E1 settlement expansion. On June 3, Hamas-Mladenov Phase 2 talks scheduled in El-Alamein, Egypt were postponed as Hamas categorically refused to surrender weapons — the precondition set by Trump's Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov for formally launching Gaza reconstruction Phase 2; only 0.5% of 42 million tons of rubble has been cleared and 77% of Gaza's population faces acute food insecurity. The IDF killed PIJ rocket cell commander Ahmed Abu Mughaysib in southern Gaza on June 3; at least 10 Palestinians were killed across Gaza on June 4 as the US Embassy in Jerusalem issued a security advisory. On June 5, Israeli settlers attacked Idhna village in the southern West Bank, beating one Palestinian and wounding another with IDF gunfire, while setting agricultural fields ablaze. Netanyahu confirmed June 4 that his heated call with Trump over a Beirut strike was real but insisted they agree on 'the main things.' The cumulative post-October 7 Palestinian death toll stands at approximately 72,950+ since October 7, 2023.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, UNICEF, NPR, Middle East Eye, CNN, The National, Euronews, CBC News, NBC News, FDD, WFP, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
